A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 10-page accounts of AnomalyAny, with matching scientific sections, equations, figures and tables. Both end with references; neither contains an appendix or the separately referenced supplementary material. The supplied content supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original anomaly-generation evaluations, downstream detection results on MVTec AD and VisA in Tables 1–3, and qualitative ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains the original generation and detection results in Tables 1–3 and the qualitative ablation results.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the same normal-sample conditioning, masked attention optimization, localization-aware scheduler and prompt-guided refinement. The losses and latent/prompt updates are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use MVTec AD and VisA, retain the same web-image generation examples, and evaluate the same anomaly-generation and 1-shot detection tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains NSA, RealNet and AnomalyDiffusion; Table 2 retains PaDiM, PatchCore, WinCLIP+, AnomalyGPT and PromptAD. Figure 7 and Table 3 retain AnomalyDiffusion, DRAEM, NSA and RealNet. DRAEM remains excluded from Table 1.

E3.justification: The reported protocols remain identical: the same generation and detection metrics, T = 100 and gamma = 0.25, foreground-mask preprocessing, and 1-shot detection using 100 generated anomalous samples. No experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The same analyses of intermediate denoising, the localization-aware scheduler, prompt detail, attention/prompt optimization and individual loss terms remain in Figures 3–5 and 8–10. Their examples and findings are unchanged.

E5.justification: Tables 2 and 3 retain the same five-run reporting and ± uncertainty entries. Neither version adds seed information, confidence intervals or significance testing relative to the other.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative results match. For example, AnomalyAny retains average IS 2.02 and IC-LPIPS 0.33 in Table 1, and image-level AUROC 94.9 ± 0.4 on MVTec AD and 89.7 ± 0.8 on VisA in Tables 2–3.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(13), including diffusion objectives, masking, attention optimization and refinement losses, are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the claims of training-free, promptable unseen anomaly generation and benefits for downstream detection. Adding 'Anomaly Anything: Promptable' to the title makes an existing capability explicit without changing claim scope.

C2.justification: The interpretations of attention guidance, prompt refinement and scheduler effects are retained. The conclusion preserves the limitations concerning CLIP's handling of lengthy or specialized descriptions and the proposed future use of anomalous-image guidance.

D1.justification: The abstract changes from promising future public source code to stating that a demo and code are available at a specified project URL. This adds concrete access information; implementation details otherwise match. The linked resources were not accessed or verified.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work discussion are unchanged, including the positioning against data-dependent anomaly generators and existing detection methods.

P1.justification: The title expands from 'Unseen Visual Anomaly Generation' to 'Anomaly Anything: Promptable Unseen Visual Anomaly Generation.' Affiliations are expanded, author email addresses are added, and the abstract's access statement is revised. The remaining prose and section order are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves from PDF page 3 to page 4, above Figure 3, with accompanying text reflow. Printed page numbers are removed, and Table 1 changes 'Bottle' to 'bottle.' The figures, table structures and displayed scientific content otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 replaces an unspecified future code release with a concrete demo/code access pointer, modestly improving reproducibility guidance. The expanded title also identifies the method and its existing promptable capability more clearly. Scientific evidence and limitations are unchanged; the benefit is limited to documentation, since the linked resources were not verified.
